reason: The text (Exodus 2:11-15) describes Hebrew suffering (סִבְלֹתָ֑ם - 'their burdens/afflictions') but contains no dialogue or statement from any leader blaming the Hebrew people for their suffering. The passage narrates Moses observing the Hebrews' burdens and his individual actions in response to witnessing an Egyptian striking a Hebrew man, followed by his flight from Egypt. No leader attributes the suffering to fault on the part of the Hebrew people.
